title: Nyquist Sampling, Aliasing & the Analog Anti-Alias Filter

blocks.x: A digital controller sees the world only at its sample instants. Anything faster than half the sample rate does not disappear - it comes back as a **slower frequency that was never there**, and no amount of digital filtering can tell the two apart afterwards. At the capstone's $1\,\text{kHz}$ tick a $1.8\,\text{kHz}$ vibration reads as $200\,\text{Hz}$, and a controller tuned to reject $200\,\text{Hz}$ will happily reject a resonance it never had. This page is the one place that arithmetic is taught; the notch filter that removes an in-band tone is `00-foundations.T2.00i`, and the uncertainty that survives sampling is `00-foundations.T2.00j`. Already know this? Take the Skip test in section 7 first.

blocks.caption: The anti-alias filter exists because every sampled wave has a slower twin at the sample rate.

blocks.x: Think of a film of a wagon wheel. The camera takes 24 pictures a second, the wheel turns faster than 12 revolutions a second, and the spokes appear to crawl backwards. Nothing is wrong with the wheel or the camera - the sampling grid is simply too coarse to represent the motion, so it reports the nearest motion it *can* represent. The alias frequency is that nearest motion, and it always lands between zero and half the frame rate.

The second half of the idea is the seam. Half the sample rate is called the **Nyquist frequency**, and it is a mirror: $3.9\,\text{kHz}$ sampled at $4\,\text{kHz}$ and $100\,\text{Hz}$ sampled at $4\,\text{kHz}$ produce exactly the same numbers. Once both are inside the same samples, only the analog filter that ran *before* the ADC can separate them.

blocks.x: where $k$ is the integer that brings the result into that interval. In code the same rule is one remainder followed by one reflection: `folded = fmod(|f|, fs)`, and if `folded > fs/2` then `folded = fs - folded`. Substituting $f = 3150\,\text{Hz}$ and $f_s = 4000\,\text{Hz}$ gives a remainder of $3150$, which is past Nyquist, so the answer is $4000 - 3150 = 850\,\text{Hz}$.

items.x: **Why a digital filter cannot undo it:** after sampling, an alias at $850\,\text{Hz}$ and a genuine $850\,\text{Hz}$ tone produce the identical sample sequence. Any filter that removes one removes the other. The only defence is **analog attenuation before the ADC** - the RC or Bessel filter from `00-foundations.T2.00h`, whose stopband starts below $f_s/2$.

blocks.x: **Predict first (before you run it):** commit to two numbers. (1) A $3150\,\text{Hz}$ switching harmonic is sampled at $f_s = 4000\,\text{Hz}$ - what frequency appears in the data? (2) A $9000\,\text{Hz}$ tone at the same rate - what frequency does *that* appear as? Two tells that a wrong answer is a mistake rather than a surprise: any alias outside $[0, 2000]\,\text{Hz}$ means the fold ran but the mirror did not, and an alias of $3150$ means neither ran.

blocks.text:
import math

fs = 4000.0
nyquist = 0.5 * fs


def alias_of(f_sig):
    folded = math.fmod(abs(f_sig), fs)
    return fs - folded if folded > nyquist else folded


alias_3150 = alias_of(3150.0)
alias_9000 = alias_of(9000.0)

assert math.isclose(nyquist, 2000.0, abs_tol=1e-12)
assert math.isclose(alias_3150, 850.0, abs_tol=1e-12)
assert math.isclose(alias_9000, 1000.0, abs_tol=1e-12)
assert 0.0 <= alias_3150 <= nyquist
print("fs=%.0f Hz | Nyquist=%.0f Hz | 3150 Hz -> %.0f Hz | 9000 Hz -> %.0f Hz"
      % (fs, nyquist, alias_3150, alias_9000))

blocks.x: Compute the alias of a $2700\,\text{Hz}$ structural resonance sampled at $f_s = 2000\,\text{Hz}$, and of a $3000\,\text{Hz}$ tone sampled at $f_s = 4000\,\text{Hz}$. Verify $700.0\,\text{Hz}$ and $1000.0\,\text{Hz}$ respectively ($\pm 10^{-9}$).

items.x: **If your result differs:** for $2700$ at $2000$ the remainder is already $700$, below Nyquist, so nothing is reflected; a result of $1300$ means the reflection ran when it should not have. For $3000$ at $4000$ the remainder is $3000$, above Nyquist, so it reflects to $4000 - 3000 = 1000$.

[`exercises/00-foundations.T2.00f/`](../exercises/00-foundations.T2.00f/) turns this section into a test. `starter.py` holds two holes: `nyquist_hz(fs)` and `alias_hz(f_sig, fs)` (fold **and** mirror). Edit it, then run the tests the way CI does:

The tests are behavioural: 3150 Hz at 4 kHz must fold to 850 Hz and 9000 Hz to 1000 Hz; 100 Hz and Nyquist itself must pass through unchanged; $3/4$ of the sample rate must mirror down to $1/4$ of it; and negative or zero sample rates must be refused rather than silently half-applied. The transfer suite drives the shared plant: the elbow's damped mode sits above 6 Hz, so a 12 Hz controller folds it to $12 - f$ while the capstone's 1 kHz tick passes it untouched. **9 tests.** Three planted faults - `alias_no_mirror`, `alias_no_fold`, `nyquist_unhalved` - each fail the test named for them, and a print-only file passes nothing (`scripts/run_exercise.py`).

items.x: **What the suite refuses.** `nyquist_hz` raises `ValueError` for a sample rate that is zero or negative, because a converter that never samples has no representable band; `alias_hz` raises `ValueError` for the same rate, so a mistyped `fs` fails loudly instead of folding everything to zero. Both refusals are tested, so a submission that returns `0.0` for a nonsense rate fails rather than passing.

items.x: **Halve the rate, then guard it.** `nyquist_hz` is `0.5 * fs`; a rate at or below zero has no band, so it raises.

**Aliasing is folding, then mirroring.** `math.fmod(2700, 2000)` already gives $700$, but $3150$ at $4000$ gives $3150$, which is above Nyquist - so subtract from $f_s$ whenever the remainder exceeds $f_s/2$.
**Check the seam.** $3000$ at $4000$ and $1000$ at $4000$ must return the same number; if they differ, the reflection is missing.
**Nyquist itself is allowed.** $2000$ at $4000$ must return $2000$, so the comparison is `>` and not `>=`.

blocks.x: Inject the `alias_no_mirror` fault: fold with `fmod` and stop there.

items.x: **Inject:** return `math.fmod(abs(f_sig), fs)` without the reflection.
**Symptom:** $3150$ at $4000$ reports $3150\,\text{Hz}$, a frequency the sampler cannot represent, while $2700$ at $2000$ still reports $700$ - so half the examples look right.
**Diagnose:** the returned value breaks the contract $0 \le f \le f_s/2$. Any output above Nyquist is proof the reflection is missing; a genuine low tone never needs one.
**Fix:** reflect with `fs - folded` when `folded > fs/2`, then assert the seam: $3000$ and $1000$ at $4\,\text{kHz}$ must agree.

items.x: `[Recall] [Concept: nyquist_sampling_and_aliasing]` A $3150\text{ Hz}$ motor switching harmonic is sampled at $f_s = 4000\text{ Hz}$ without an anti-aliasing filter. What alias frequency $f_{\text{alias}} \in [0, 2000]\text{ Hz}$ (tolerance $\pm 10^{-9}$) appears in the digital data?
`[Apply] [Concept: nyquist_sampling_and_aliasing]` A $3900\text{ Hz}$ tone is sampled at $f_s = 4000\text{ Hz}$. Compute its alias in $\text{Hz}$ (tolerance $\pm 10^{-9}$).
`[Transfer] [Concept: nyquist_sampling_and_aliasing]` Why can no digital filter recover a $3150\text{ Hz}$ tone that was sampled at $4000\text{ Hz}$ without an analog filter?
**A.** Because digital filters only work below $100\text{ Hz}$.

**B.** Because the samples of the $3150\text{ Hz}$ tone are identical to those of an $850\text{ Hz}$ tone, so removing one removes the other; only an analog filter ahead of the ADC can tell them apart.
**C.** Because the ADC needs double-precision floating point.
**D.** Because folding amplifies high frequencies.
`[Concept: nyquist_sampling_and_aliasing]` A tone arrives at exactly $f_s/2$. What does the sampler report?
**A.** Nothing: the converter refuses to digitise it.
**B.** Exactly $f_s/2$, but its phase is unrecoverable, so the reading is ambiguous.
**C.** Zero, because the tone sits on the seam.
**D.** $f_s$, because the mirror doubles it.

`[Spaced review -> 00-foundations.T2.00e — Concept: continuous_state_space_matrices]` For $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -100 & -4 \end{bmatrix}$, compute $\operatorname{tr}(A)$ (tolerance $\pm 10^{-9}$).

assert math.isclose(q1_alias_hz, 850.0, rel_tol=1e-9)
assert math.isclose(q2_alias_hz, 100.0, rel_tol=1e-9)
assert q3_choice == "B"
assert q4_choice == "B"
assert math.isclose(q5_review, -4.0, rel_tol=1e-9, abs_tol=1e-9)
